A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H are sitting around a square table facing centre, but not necessarily in the same order.

A and F are sitting at the corners. H is not sitting at the corner.

Statement I: C is to the second right of H. G is to the second right of A.

No definite arrangement can be established.

So, statement I alone is not sufficient.

Statement II: D is facing H. A is facing B, who is to the immediate left of C.

So, either none or four persons are sitting between A and H when counted in the clockwise direction from A.

So, statement II alone is not sufficient.

By combining I and II:

D is facing H. A is facing B, who is to the immediate left of C.

C is to the second right of H. G is to the second right of A.

F is sitting at the corner.

So, four persons are sitting between A and H when counted in the clockwise direction from A.

Thus, statements I and II together are sufficient.
